newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares down two pct on rate, dlr worries.
newsitem.headline: German shares down two pct on rate, dlr worries.

text.p: German shares stumbled badly at the open on Tuesday, falling nearly two percent as traders braced for the Federal Reserve's decision on interest rates later and a weaker dollar hurt export-related companies.
The blue-chip DAX index was down 70.52 points, or 1.96 percent, in early floor trade to 3,534.03 points.
Aside from worries about higher U.S. interest rates, traders said the weaker dollar was taking a toll a export-related companies, especially chemical firms.
Hoechst AG, for example, was 1.90 to 65.60 marks while Bayer fell 1.67 to 64.15 marks.
Shares in BASF AG, meanwhile, fell 2.82 to 63.25 marks after news emerged over the weekend that it faces an $8.5 billion lawsuit in the U.S.
Shares in Deutsche Telekom AG also came under pressure, falling 1.30 marks to 38.45, amid profit-taking as a tax break on trading the shares took effect.
Under German law, investors can sell shares in a company without having to pay a capital gains if they hold the shares for six months.

Shares in Deutsche Bank AG, meanwhile, were 1.80 lower at 96.90 marks after the bank said first quarter profit climbed 28 percent to 1.4 billion marks and that the results confirmed its forecast of higher profit for the year as a whole.
